days.title: An RV32I Subset and Its Datapath Contract

questions.prompt: Which statement about RV32I ADD belongs to the architectural contract rather than this course's implementation?
options: It must pass through one physical ripple-carry adder.
It writes the low 32 bits of rs1 + rs2 to rd, with a write to x0 having no retained effect.
It must complete in one clock cycle.
It must use separate instruction and data memories.
questions.explanation: The ISA specifies the visible 32-bit result and x0 behavior. Adder structure, cycle count, and memory-port organization are microarchitectural choices.

questions.prompt: Why is this lesson's chosen instruction set called a subset rather than a new ISA?
options: Every included operation retains its official RV32I encoding and behavior; the lesson merely omits other instructions.
The Python model is allowed to redefine included instructions.
The subset replaces RISC-V registers with host Python variables architecturally.
A subset must contain every privileged instruction but no integer instruction.
questions.explanation: Selecting fewer official instructions narrows what the teaching core implements. It does not permit changing the semantics of an instruction that remains included.

questions.prompt: For an S-type SW instruction, what role do instruction bits 11:7 have?
options: They always name the destination register.
They select a hidden condition-code register.
They hold the low five bits of the split store immediate.
They encode the physical cache set.
questions.explanation: Field locations can be extracted uniformly, but their meaning depends on format. In S-type, bits 11:7 contribute immediate bits and there is no rd.

questions.prompt: Which item is microarchitectural state rather than architectural RV32I integer state?
options: The value visible in x5
The current instruction-address state
A byte written by an architecturally completed SW
A cache-line valid bit
questions.explanation: Cache metadata exists because of one implementation's memory hierarchy. Software-visible registers, sequencing, and completed memory effects belong to the architectural model.

days.title: ALU, Register File, and Program Counter

questions.prompt: For bit patterns a=0xffffffff and b=1, what do SLT and SLTU respectively produce?
options: SLT produces 1 because signed -1 < 1; SLTU produces 0 because unsigned 0xffffffff is greater than 1.
Both produce 1 because the bit patterns are identical inputs.
SLT produces 0 and SLTU produces 1 because sign is stored in the register file.
Both raise an integer-overflow exception.
questions.explanation: Registers hold bit patterns without a permanent signed type. The selected operation supplies signed or unsigned interpretation; neither comparison raises overflow.

questions.prompt: Why does the lab enforce x0 both when reading and when accepting writes?
options: RV32I requires x0 to preserve the most recent discarded value.
Reads must always return zero, while attempted writes must have no architectural effect.
The OS periodically resets x0 between instructions.
The ALU cannot operate when either source register is zero.
questions.explanation: The two paths express both halves of the invariant. A physical implementation can omit row zero, but its observable behavior must remain the same.

questions.prompt: What happens in the lab when x5 contains 7 and a rising edge writes 9 to x5?
options: The combinational read shows 9 before the edge.
The read remains 7 permanently because reads are combinational.
The read shows 7 before the edge and 9 after the nonblocking state update.
The write is architecturally forbidden because source and destination names match.
questions.explanation: The register file's read is combinational from retained state, while the write changes that state at the edge. Actual memory macros can require explicit bypass for related timing cases.

questions.prompt: Which description of the PC path is most precise?
options: The PC increments itself automatically after decode.
The compiler writes the PC register after every instruction.
A branch target replaces the current PC before comparison.
Combinational logic forms candidates such as pc+4 and a target; control selects one for the PC register to capture.
questions.explanation: The PC is state. Adders and target logic form candidate values, selection chooses one, and a clocked update retains it.

questions.prompt: Why is recognizing only the seven-bit major opcode insufficient to validate every instruction in the lesson subset?
options: funct3 and sometimes funct7 distinguish legal operations and widths inside an opcode family.
The opcode exists only after register writeback.
Every major opcode identifies exactly one instruction on all RISC-V systems.
Legality is determined by the cache replacement policy.
questions.explanation: For families such as OP and LOAD, function fields select the exact operation. Ignoring them can turn an unsupported encoding into an unintended architectural write.

questions.prompt: For LW in the single-cycle datapath, which combination is correct?
options: ALU B selects rs2, memory is written, and writeback selects pc+4.
ALU B selects the sign-extended immediate, memory is read, and writeback selects loaded data.
The branch target is used as the data address and no register is written.
The immediate selects a physical page-table entry directly.
questions.explanation: LW adds rs1 to its I-type immediate to form the effective address, reads data memory, and writes the returned word to rd.

questions.prompt: Why should the decoder's illegal default deassert register and memory write enables?
options: It makes every unknown word a valid NOP in official RISC-V.
It reduces the number of instruction fields.
It prevents unsupported encodings from committing accidental architectural effects before a real trap mechanism handles them.
It guarantees physical timing closure.
questions.explanation: Failing closed protects architectural state. A complete core would also report an illegal-instruction exception; silently executing arbitrary controls is incorrect.

questions.prompt: Why can a load determine the clock period of a textbook single-cycle core?
options: Every ADD is translated through the page table twice.
Loads are the only instructions with an opcode.
The OS schedules one process per load.
The load path can cross instruction fetch, decode/register read, address addition, data memory, and writeback before one capture edge.
questions.explanation: The global period must accommodate the longest enabled register-to-register path. Faster instructions still wait for that same edge in this design.

days.title: Integrating and Running a Tiny RV32I Core

questions.prompt: What distinguishes a combinational candidate from an architectural state update in the tiny core?
options: Candidates are calculated from current state; only enabled writes and the selected next PC are retained at the commit boundary.
Every candidate changes memory as soon as Python evaluates it.
Architectural state exists only in assembly source.
Candidates are OS policy, while state is cache policy.
questions.explanation: The model first derives ALU, memory, branch, writeback, and next-PC values without mutation. Its clock method then commits the enabled architectural changes.

questions.prompt: Why does the included four-element loop execute 25 model cycles?
options: Every instruction takes five pipeline stages.
Three setup instructions run once, five loop instructions run four times, and two final memory instructions run once.
The data cache misses exactly 25 times.
The branch is taken four times and flushes one instruction each time.
questions.explanation: The count is 3 + (5 × 4) + 2 = 25. This Day 4 model commits one instruction per abstract cycle and does not yet model a pipeline or cache.

questions.prompt: The second array word is -2 and is stored as bytes fe ff ff ff. What does LW place in the register?
options: A Python negative integer that is not a 32-bit pattern
Only the low byte 0xfe
The 32-bit pattern 0xfffffffe reconstructed in little-endian order
A sign flag plus the magnitude 2
questions.explanation: LW reconstructs four little-endian bytes into a 32-bit pattern. Signed display or signed operations interpret those bits later; the register has no persistent signed tag.

questions.prompt: Why is the model stopping on a misaligned LW not yet evidence of a modeled RISC-V trap?
options: RISC-V defines no memory exceptions.
Misalignment can be detected only by Linux.
Python exceptions are architecturally identical to machine traps.
The model lacks trap CSRs, a saved faulting PC/cause, privilege transition, trap vector, and restart path.
questions.explanation: A host-language error safely stops the lab but does not implement the architectural exception mechanism that systems software depends on.

questions.prompt: For stage delays 180, 220, 250, 210, and 140 ps with 60 ps register/clock overhead, what is the modeled pipeline clock period?
options: 310 ps
200 ps
questions.explanation: The period is bounded by the slowest stage plus boundary overhead: max(180,220,250,210,140) + 60 = 310 ps.

questions.prompt: Why can the five-stage pipeline improve throughput while one instruction's time latency increases?
options: It removes stages from each instruction.
Different instructions overlap in different stages, but one instruction still crosses all stages and pays each boundary.
It executes every dependence simultaneously.
It changes the ISA to permit approximate results.
questions.explanation: Overlap raises completion rate after filling. In the lesson numbers, one instruction takes 5 × 310 = 1550 ps, longer than the 1060 ps single-cycle path.

questions.prompt: How many ideal cycles do N independent instructions require in a k-stage pipeline, including fill and drain?
options: N/k
kN
k + N - 1
N - k
questions.explanation: The first instruction needs k stages, and each subsequent independent instruction can finish one cycle later in the ideal single-issue model.

questions.prompt: Why must an interstage register carry rd, controls, and validity with a computed value?
options: The ISA requires software to read pipeline registers.
It reduces every stage's physical delay to zero.
The OS uses rd as a cache tag.
Later stages must know which instruction owns the value, what effect is allowed, and whether the stage contains real work.
questions.explanation: A number alone cannot say whether to write a register, access memory, report an exception, or do nothing. Identity and valid/kill metadata preserve ownership.

questions.prompt: What makes add x5,x1,x2 followed by sub x6,x5,x3 a RAW dependence?
options: The younger SUB must read the value the older ADD produces in x5.
Both instructions write x5.
The ADD reads a value that the SUB will later overwrite.
Both instructions require a page-table walk.
questions.explanation: The data flow is write x5 then read x5. The chosen pipeline must forward or stall so the consumer receives the producer's value.

questions.prompt: Why does an immediately dependent ALU instruction often stall one cycle after LW even when forwarding exists?
options: Loads never produce register values.
The loaded data becomes available near the end of MEM, after the consumer would need it at the start of EX.
Forwarding can operate only on x0.
The OS must approve each bypass.
questions.explanation: Forwarding cannot send a value backward in time. The interlock delays the consumer until the load data exists and can be bypassed.

questions.prompt: Why do WAR and WAW names not require stalls in this lesson's single-issue in-order five-stage pipeline?
options: RISC-V forbids two instructions from naming one register.
Register renaming is mandatory in every RV32I implementation.
Reads and writes occur in order, so their timing cannot invert in this pipeline.
WAR and WAW apply only to memory addresses.
questions.explanation: The dependencies exist as name relationships, but this schedule performs ID reads and WB writes in order. Out-of-order timing can make false dependencies operationally important.

questions.prompt: After a predict-not-taken branch resolves as taken in EX, what must happen to younger sequential-path instructions?
options: They must retire before the branch.
They become kernel instructions.
Their register writes are allowed but stores are blocked.
They are invalidated and prevented from committing any architectural effect while fetch redirects to the target.
questions.explanation: Prediction may start speculative work but cannot change the ISA result. Recovery kills all wrong-path effects and redirects the front end.

days.title: Cache, TLB, MMU, and End-to-End Task Trace

questions.prompt: A user load misses in the TLB, and a hardware walk finds a valid user-readable leaf PTE. What can happen without an OS trap?
options: The walker can fill the TLB and retry or continue the load using the translated physical address.
The task must be terminated because every TLB miss is a page fault.
The data cache may return any line with the same virtual offset.
The compiler must emit a replacement load.
questions.explanation: A TLB miss means only that cached translation is absent. A successful hardware walk can restore the fast path without raising an architectural page-fault exception.

questions.prompt: Why can a store to VA 0x4004 fault even after a load brought its physical cache line into the D-cache?
options: A cache line can never be written after being read.
Cache residency does not grant permission; the translation metadata can permit reads while denying writes.
Every D-cache hit causes a protection exception.
Stores require the same bytes to be present in the I-cache.
questions.explanation: Permission checking is part of translation/protection and must precede use of cached data. A cache hit cannot bypass OS-configured read-only policy.

questions.prompt: With 4 KiB pages, which virtual-address portion remains unchanged when an ordinary PTE replaces the VPN with a PPN?
options: The complete virtual page number
The ASID
The low 12-bit page offset
The cache tag
questions.explanation: Translation selects a physical page while preserving the byte position within that page, so PA = (PPN << 12) | offset.

questions.prompt: Which responsibility assignment is correct for the C sum trace?
options: The ISA chooses cache replacement and the OS chooses transistor widths.
The TLB stores array values and the D-cache stores process permissions.
The MMU decides whether Linux should kill a process.
The ISA defines visible instruction effects; microarchitecture implements caches and stalls; the OS creates mappings and handles faults; physical circuits move charge.
questions.explanation: The four layers cooperate but own different decisions. Hardware reports and enforces architectural mechanisms; the kernel supplies policy; physical devices realize the implementation.
